strategies.rationale: Public win-probability and Expected Points Added (EPA) models consistently show NFL coaches punt and kick field goals far too conservatively, relinquishing measurable expected points per game.
strategies.recommendation: Adopt aggressive 4th-down go-for-it rules, consistently attempting conversions on 4th-and-3 or shorter past your own 40-yard line and 4th-and-1 anywhere on the field. Eliminate low-value punts and long field goal attempts in these neutral-to-favorable midfield zones.
strategies.title: Aggressive 4th-Down Conversion Decision Rules

strategies.rationale: Extensive public analytics confirms motion at the snap boosts offensive EPA per play and success rate by revealing coverage indicators and weakening defensive gap integrity.
strategies.recommendation: Incorporate pre-snap or at-the-snap motion on over 75% of offensive dropbacks and runs, prioritizing motion at the snap. Use late motion intentionally to force real-time coverage communication and compromise secondary leverage.
strategies.title: High-Volume Pre-Snap and Snap-Motion Usage

strategies.rationale: Public analytics is silent on offensive momentum and psychological disruption via timeouts. Coaching judgment indicates stopping fast-paced opponent drives prevents compounding multi-play defensive collapses.
strategies.recommendation: Call a defensive timeout early in the 3rd quarter whenever the opponent completes consecutive 15+ yard plays, explicitly breaking offensive play-calling tempo. Use the stoppage to reset defensive personnel and calm panic.
strategies.title: Early Second-Half Timeout Calls for Momentum Interruption

strategies.rationale: Public analytics focuses almost exclusively on double-teaming WR1s; coaching intuition suggests taking away safety-valve secondary options creates QB hesitation that quantitative models do not capture.
strategies.recommendation: Bracket and double-team the opponent's WR2 or TE1 on 3rd-and-medium, while leaving the WR1 in single coverage with safety leverage to disrupt timing. Force the QB to move off their quick second read into unfamiliar late progressions.
